      Territory map

      Flagged accounts by location · dot size = 12-month spend
      Rep visitAI callAuto offer
      1 · IdentifyBroken rhythm, not a fixed cut-offEach account is compared against its own normal order interval. Churn = silent for more than 3× its usual gap.
      2 · PrioritiseRisk × valueA transparent 0–100 risk score from four signals, multiplied by a spend score. Ties are broken by 12-month spend.
      3 · ActOne action per accountA playbook per situation (win-back, service recovery, rhythm rescue, category recovery), delivered through visit, AI call or automated offer.

      Churn definition

      Accounts here are zip-code areas. Order volume grows strongly through 2017, so a fixed rule like "no order in 90 days" punishes slow buyers and misses fast ones. We measure gap ratio = days since last order ÷ the account's average gap between orders.

      At risk: gap ratio above 2 (or a sharp drop in order frequency). Churned: gap ratio above 3. Scope: the 2,611 accounts with 10+ orders, which place 52% of all orders and have a stable baseline. Smaller accounts show too many random gaps.

      Evidence (backtest)

      We set "today" to 28 Feb 2018 and checked which accounts with 10+ orders placed no order between March and August 2018.

      A 60%+ drop in order frequency over 90 days gives 28% churn, against 3% for accounts without a drop. Late deliveries and low reviews barely predict churn at account level, so they carry a small weight in the score. Their main use is in the conversation: they tell the rep how to open the call.

      Risk score (0–100)

      SignalMeasureMax pts
      Order rhythmGap ratio: <1 → 0 · 1–1.5 → 5 · 1.5–2 → 15 · 2–3 → 25 · >3 → 3535
      Frequency declineOrders in last 90 days vs the 90 days before25
      SatisfactionAverage review score per account10
      DeliveryShare of orders delivered late10

      Total of 80 points, normalised to 100. Tiers: High ≥ 70 · Medium 40–69 · Low < 40.

      Priority

      Priority = risk score × spend score (1–5, spend quintiles). A 95%-risk account worth R$ 300 matters less than a 75%-risk account worth R$ 20,000.

      Revenue at risk = 12-month spend × churn probability for the account's gap-ratio band, taken from the backtest.

      Coverage rule (per territory, per week)

      Top 10 by priority → rep visit · next 25 → AI voice call (ElevenLabs agent, hands unhappy accounts to the rep) · remaining High/Medium → automated offer · Low → monitor only.

      Does the score work? Backtest of the full risk score

      We rebuilt the exact score as of 28 Feb 2018, using only data up to that day, and then checked who stopped ordering over the next six months. 1,258 accounts, of which 88 churned (7.0%).

      High tier churned52%7.4× the 7% average
      Top 10% flagged47%of all accounts that later churned
      Ranking accuracy (AUC)0.770.5 = coin flip · 1.0 = perfect
      Top 20% by priority60%of the spend that was lost

      Second test from 31 Dec 2017: the High tier churned at 50% (8.7×), AUC 0.70. Order rhythm and frequency drive the result. Removing the review and delivery points gives the same accuracy, so those points mainly guide how the rep opens the conversation. Script: Backtest/backtest.py.

      Product lines

      As the brief suggests, marketplace categories are read as lines in a drinks portfolio: health_beauty → Premium Lager, bed_bath_table → Core Lager, computers_accessories → 0.0 Non-Alcoholic, sports_leisure → Cider, furniture_decor → Craft & Specialty, and so on.

      Student prototype for the HEINEKEN × AISO challenge (UvA, Theories of Business Intelligence Technology). Not an official HEINEKEN tool. Data: about 91k anonymised marketplace orders (Jan 2017–Aug 2018), with zip-code areas treated as on-trade accounts. Offers, scripts and messages are generated from each account's own signals.
